findings: The route comment in infra/routes.yaml says admin protection 'relies on the internal network for isolation,' but infra/network.yaml sets `api-service.public: true`, directly contradicting that assumption — /admin/refund is reachable straight from the public internet with no network-layer restriction backing it up.

The only access control on POST /admin/refund is comparing the client-supplied `x-internal-role` header to the literal string 'admin'; since infra/routes.yaml attaches no auth middleware to /admin/* and the upstream service is publicly reachable, any external caller can simply set that header themselves and pass the check, gaining full admin refund capability with zero real authentication.

processRefund(req.body.orderId, req.body.amount) is invoked directly from unvalidated request-body fields — there's no check that orderId refers to a real/owned order or that amount is positive, bounded, or matches the order's actual value, so a spoofed request can refund an arbitrary amount to an arbitrary order.

There is no idempotency key or replay protection around the refund call, so a single spoofed request (or a legitimate one) can be resent repeatedly to trigger duplicate refunds against the same order.

No audit logging or caller-identity capture surrounds the refund action — nothing records which client/service invoked processRefund, so abuse via the spoofed header would leave no trail for detection or incident response.
